## Implemented

Queued work remains a scheduler reservation until capacity is acquired and fresh admission succeeds. Every runTask path (initial work, graph/tracker top-up, review re-entry, RESOLVE retry and stack-conflict retry) checks integration hold, start gate, quarantine/retry state and effective dependencies before starting an attempt. Rejection releases the slot in finally, records its admission reason and produces no implementation/fix/merge outcome.

Local implementation nodes retain completed/implDone early-unblock behavior, including a freshly implemented RESOLVE retry parent. External review/blocker/gate/epic/task dependencies use authoritative tracker closure through compact top-up observations. Failed, missing, duplicate or malformed observations invalidate only the affected dependency. Opaque candidates use tracker-ready membership. Queued external/opaque work refreshes facts after capacity; exhausted query budget holds work requiring fresh observations.

One timer at a configurable 30-second default cadence shares the existing serialized top-up and finite topUpQueryCap. External releases can be observed during unrelated in-flight implementation. Queries never await task chains or the merge lane, and quiescence cancels the timer. The detector remains nonnegative after rejected initial reservations. Both coordinator documents carry the same operative protocol.

## Verification

Final tested source: 214a28e8c1dba33b026db6441fd97ef27af55d59 on integration base b635541015f4bc0e037ef8621f8d01135ca2b22b. Final head adds only the retained post-rebase evidence file; `git diff --exit-code 214a28e8c1dba33b026db6441fd97ef27af55d59 HEAD -- skills/super-code/coordinator.js skills/super-code/coordinator-workflow.md skills/super-code/coordinator-subagents.md tests/super-code/replay-harness.mjs` exited 0. `git diff --check` passed and final `git status --short` was empty.


Output: `1900 passed, 0 failed` (exit 0). This includes the existing three documented dryRun scenarios, live-sim prompt generation, early-unblock/retry/cancellation contracts, and the new admission/readiness fixtures. Retained task excerpt and verdict: `evidence/super-plan-ufz.3/replay-post-rebase.txt`.

New cases prove:

- An integration hold established while a consumer waits for a slot prevents its implementation, review, fix and merge, with no attempt ledger entry.
- A post-capacity tracker observation holds an external-review consumer and releases the slot to unrelated work.
- External review closure releases a consumer before an unrelated long implementation finishes; the review ID never enters local completed.
- Open human gates, open blockers and an unavailable lookup hold their consumers with explicit reasons while unrelated work progresses.
- Fake cadence drives refresh deterministically; calls remain within the query cap and no fake timer remains at quiescence.
- The mechanical generated prompt requests authoritative status/kind observations and preserves independent lookup errors. Both Workflow and ordinary-subagent contracts were inspected; live ordinary-subagent behavior evaluation remains parent-owned.

The assertions can fail on concrete wrong behavior: an impl/review/fix/merge dispatch for a rejected ID; missing unrelated completion after slot rejection; consumer dispatch after the long task finishes; an open-gate/blocker/unavailable consumer dispatch; missing dependency error text; query count above its cap; or an outstanding timer.

# super-plan-ufz.8.2 implementation evidence

Status: IMPLEMENTED

## Implementation

Added `report-verdict --complete --source IMMUTABLE_SOURCE_ID FILE` as a separate additive parser branch. The existing default and `--keys` parser branches are unchanged. The new mode emits one JSON object and exits 0 only after validating the entire recognized finding source; errors exit 2 with a stderr diagnostic and no success JSON.

Complete extraction includes final-review Must fix, Untested scope and Deferred OK; task-report concern/blocker/finding and deferred sections, even with a success status; and roast Confirmed findings of every severity, both Not verified routes, Beyond remainder cap count evidence, Rejected with reason, Unverified nits, Escalations and deferred sections. It retains duplicate appearances and multiline continuations, without legacy item or text caps. It does not store, match, resolve, route, amend or project findings.

## Interface for super-plan-ufz.8.4

CLI: `bash skills/super-code/scripts/report-verdict --complete --source '<immutable invocation/logical-artifact identity>' '<actual report path>'`

Schema: `{version:1,source,artifact,kind,verdict,occurrences:[{section,position,key,text}]}`.

- `source`: the supplied immutable string verbatim; required, nonblank, no ASCII control characters. The caller owns the immutable identity promise. This extractor does not derive identity from the file path or infer semantic equivalence.
- `artifact`: FILE exactly as supplied; may change when the source is archived.
- `kind`: `final-review`, `roast`, or `task-report`, selected using the existing recognition priority (exact `## Verdict` wins over quoted task Status).
- `verdict`: full recognized verdict without the compact summary's truncation.
- `section`: exact source heading/label text with its Markdown heading/bold delimiter removed. A bold label's colon remains part of the label, consistent with existing label parsing. No case or wording normalization is applied.
- `position`: 1-based appearance position within that exact section label, accumulated across repeated headings with the same label. Duplicate finding text remains separate. `none` markers do not consume occurrence positions.
- `key`: original first item line without its Markdown list marker. For roast items, only the portion before the first ` — ` is the key. Markdown emphasis and Unicode are retained.
- `text`: original first item line without its list marker, followed by original continuation lines (including indentation, nested bullets, emphasis and internal blank lines). Trailing separator blank lines are excluded. CRLF/CR are normalized to LF; neither text nor key is capped.
- The occurrence identity is `(source,section,position)`, not `(artifact,section,position)`. An archive copied byte for byte and parsed with the same source has exactly the same occurrences.

Missing/non-file/unreadable paths, unknown/unsupported source formats, invalid UTF-8, missing verdict/sections, empty finding sections, and unmarked leading finding text fail explicitly. ## Implementation

PR assembly resolves `--base` and `--head` once with `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`. Task review carries the implementer's head as `[HEAD]`; packages, test diffs, source reads, and base recovery use captured commits. Seam review uses the merge report's head, and check-fix review uses the fixer's head. Task review retains its existing no-test-run policy.

The existing Finish ledger-read dispatch captures verified `reviewBase`/`reviewHead` fields alongside its text. Assembly, final single/cluster/seam reviews, and direct-input assembler fallbacks consume that same pair. Failed or missing capture leaves an explicit unavailable review with evidence; it never falls back to moving refs. There is no new dispatch or workflow engine. The documented dryRun call counts remain 48, 19, and 23.

The ordinary CLI carries explicit `--head` for task and check-fix review, and `--base`/`--head` for review assembly and final reviews; equivalent Launch `reviewBase`/`reviewHead` values are supported. Moving source refs are rejected at that boundary. History/assess callers retain their existing inputs.

Existing review prompt blocks permit unique review-owned detached worktrees when a filesystem view is needed and separate mutable output/temp directories for reproductions. They keep caller checkouts read-only and describe caller commit/status differences as evidence without assigning causality from differences alone or restoring an old snapshot.

It verifies commit objects; uses argument-array Git operations, literal pathspecs and NUL-delimited enumeration; discovers collection records in tracked `run.md` files at the captured endpoints; derives archives from each record's own directory and safe invocation identity; and checks saved SHA-256 against captured regular-file blobs. It never reads a producer workspace or mutable run file for selection.

Only exact manifest-claimed assembled input files and invocation direct `.md.diff` payloads can be omitted. Unclaimed descendants, ordinary `reviews` content, collection metadata and final/cluster reports remain in the selected range. The selected list, diffstat and deterministic path-to-slice mapping are emitted with explicit captured record/invocation/archive/report/hash provenance. Ordinal slice names support unusual/long paths and avoid collisions; the recursion correction is verified exact payload selection, not filename shortening alone. The original captured BASE/HEAD is preserved.

Malformed/conflicting records, incomplete claimed bundles, missing/non-regular claimed files and hash mismatches produce an explicit unavailable sidecar and no omission authority. Inspecting prior endpoint claims also catches removed/corrupted payloads even when their record disappears. No record grants no exemption; untracked archives supply neither input nor authority. Historical archive bytes are never rewritten.

Both review profiles use this operation through the existing shared `assemblePrompt` builder. The digest includes generated-input provenance; semantic import/call clustering, digest extraction and size checks remain assembler-owned. Selection refusal follows the existing unavailable path and prevents a clean fallback result, in Workflow routing and the shared ordinary final-review prompt. Super-auto's roast fallback retains the same explicit gap. History/assess and general direct review-package behavior remain unchanged. `report-status` required no source edit: its existing path/hash manifest and derived archive identity already supply all reader provenance.

## Current outcome

Implemented the assessment-backed existing-component boundary in `dispatch-text.mjs`. Its additive `review-inputs --ledger ... --base <full captured commit> --head <full captured commit> --out-dir ...` mode exits before loading coordinator builders. It verifies commit objects; uses argument-array Git operations, literal pathspecs and NUL-delimited enumeration; discovers collection records in tracked `run.md` files at the captured endpoints; derives archives from each record's own directory and safe invocation identity; and checks saved SHA-256 against captured regular-file blobs. It never reads a producer workspace or mutable run file for selection.

Only exact manifest-claimed assembled input files and invocation direct `.md.diff` payloads can be omitted. Unclaimed descendants, ordinary `reviews` content, collection metadata and final/cluster reports remain in the selected range. The selected list, diffstat and deterministic path-to-slice mapping are emitted with explicit captured record/invocation/archive/report/hash provenance. Ordinal slice names support unusual/long paths and avoid collisions; the recursion correction is verified exact payload selection, not filename shortening alone. The original captured BASE/HEAD is preserved.

Malformed/conflicting records, incomplete claimed bundles, missing/non-regular claimed files and hash mismatches produce an explicit unavailable sidecar and no omission authority. Inspecting prior endpoint claims also catches removed/corrupted payloads even when their record disappears. No record grants no exemption; untracked archives supply neither input nor authority. Historical archive bytes are never rewritten.

Both review profiles use this operation through the existing shared `assemblePrompt` builder. The digest includes generated-input provenance; semantic import/call clustering, digest extraction and size checks remain assembler-owned. Selection refusal follows the existing unavailable path and prevents a clean fallback result, in Workflow routing and the shared ordinary final-review prompt. Super-auto's roast fallback retains the same explicit gap. History/assess and general direct review-package behavior remain unchanged. `report-status` required no source edit: its existing path/hash manifest and derived archive identity already supply all reader provenance.

The isolated branch was rebased cleanly onto current integration `c3fac4369c7c737e2e7f9f7250fd253b21442d12` (integration advanced beyond the originally named `7c3fec35`).
